task_completion.description: GeoGebra application is open and the ground line and wheel (circle or arc) are constructed.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GeoGebra workspace is visible showing a horizontal line (ground) and a circle/arc representing the wheel.

task_completion.description: The bike is oriented facing LEFT and the wheel radius is set to 370 mm.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The wheel is on the left side of the steering axis. The Algebra view or a label shows a radius or circle equation consistent with 370 units.

task_completion.description: The steering axis is constructed with a 67-degree angle from the horizontal ground and a 44 mm offset.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A line representing the steering axis is visible. The Algebra view or angle tool shows 67 degrees. The distance between the wheel center and the steering axis (offset) is 44 mm.

task_completion.description: The distance between the wheel's contact point and the steering axis intercept on the ground is measured.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A segment or distance measurement is visible on the ground line between the point directly under the wheel center and the point where the steering axis hits the ground.

task_completion.description: A text box is added to the workspace displaying the calculated Trail value.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A text element is visible in the GeoGebra window saying 'Trail = [value] mm' (value should be approx 109.26).

task_completion.description: The project is saved with the specific filename in the correct directory.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The GeoGebra title bar or a file explorer window shows the file 'bicycle_trail.ggb' in the ~/Documents/GeoGebra/projects/ path.

integrity.description: The agent used the GeoGebra GUI tools rather than just typing the final answer.
integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with GeoGebra tools (point, line, circle, measurement) or the input bar within the app.

integrity.description: The trail value is derived from geometric construction, not just a typed text box without supporting lines.
integrity.visual_evidence: The Algebra view shows the geometric dependencies (intersections, segments, angles) used to calculate the trail.

integrity.description: The agent interacted with the actual GeoGebra software interface.
integrity.visual_evidence: The standard GeoGebra toolbar, Algebra view, and Graphics view are visible and active.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The wheel radius must be 370 mm. The head tube angle is 67 degrees from the horizontal. The fork rake (offset) is 44 mm. The mathematically correct Ground Trail for these parameters is approximately 109.26 mm (acceptable range: 107.26 mm to 111.26 mm). The bike must face LEFT, meaning the steering axis intercept on the ground should be to the LEFT of the wheel's contact point.
